```{r include=FALSE}
library(diyar)
```
Many epidemiological case definitions distinguish new occurrences from repeat events.
This is commonly done by specifying a period from an index event within 
which other events are considered part of the same occurrence.

This vignette introduces how this is done with `episodes()`.

We begin by reviewing `event_dt` below. 
This is a sample dataset of 11 infection events and includes
data on the location and type of infection.
```{r warning=FALSE}
tmp.seed <- 3
event_dt <- seq(from = as.Date("2021-01-01"), to = as.Date("2021-01-11"), by = 1)
event_dt <- data.frame(date = event_dt)
event_dt$attr_1 <- 
  c("BSI", "UTI", "RTI", "RTI", "BSI", "BSI", "BSI", "RTI", "RTI", "BSI", "RTI")
event_dt$attr_2 <- 
  c("Ward 1", "Ward 1", "Ward 3", "Ward 3", "Ward 2", "Ward 2", 
    "Ward 1", "Ward 1", "Ward 3","Ward 3", "Ward 2")
event_dt$dur <- 10
event_dt$dur[event_dt$attr_1 == 'UTI'] <- 7
event_dt$dur[event_dt$attr_1 == 'RTI'] <- 3

event_dt
```

The simplest implementations of `episodes()` are shown below. 
Episodes can also be created separately 
within subsets (`strata`) of dataset.

```{r warning=FALSE}
# A single episode  
event_dt$ep1a <- episodes(
  event_dt$date, episode_type = "fixed", group_stats = 'case_nm')
# Episodes created separately by infection type
event_dt$ep1b <- episodes(
  event_dt$date, episode_type = "fixed", group_stats = 'case_nm', 
  strata = event_dt$attr_1)
# Episodes created separately by location
event_dt$ep1c <- episodes(
  event_dt$date, episode_type = "fixed", group_stats = 'case_nm', 
  strata = event_dt$attr_2)

event_dt
```

`episodes()` creates a group identifier for each occurrence.
This occurrence is referred to as an episode. The index event is categorised as 
the case `(C)`, while other events are categorised as duplicates `(D)`
of that case. The group identifier is an `S4` (`epid`) class with useful 
information about each group in its slots. These information can be accessed 
with `as.data.frame()` or `as.list()`.

We can implement more complex case definitions by changing different aspects of 
the episode tracking process. These are explained below. 

# Type of episodes
## Fixed episodes  
These are episodes where a fixed period from the index case is used to 
distinguish one occurrence of an outcome from another. Events that occur
outside of this fixed period (relative to the index event) are 
classified as separate episodes and given different group IDs.

In the example below, every event after the fourth day will be 
assigned to a different episode, each with its own case event. 
```{r warning=FALSE}
# 3-day difference fixed episodes 
event_dt$ep2 <- episodes(
  event_dt$date, case_length = 3, episode_type = "fixed", 
  group_stats = 'case_nm')
```

## Rolling episodes
For rolling episodes, the duration distinguishing one occurrence from another is 
not fixed. Instead, it is continuously extended if a new event falls within the
recurrence window. This chaining process continues indefinitely until there are
no more events within the recurrence window or it is
stopped by the `rolls_max` argument.

```{r warning=FALSE}
# 3-day difference rolling episodes 
event_dt$ep3 <- episodes(
  event_dt$date, case_length = 3, episode_type = "rolling", 
  group_stats = 'case_nm')
event_dt
```

In the example above, we see the introduction of recurrent events `(R)`.
A recurrent event is the first event within the recurrent window and 
categorised separately from duplicate events `(D)`. 

Note that `case_length` and `recurrence_length` are interpreted as 
unit-differences. For example, a `case_length` of `3` is means a difference 
of 3 units (see `help(epid_unit)`) between event dates, not 3 calendar days between 
events.

# Selecting index events
We can control which record is used as the reference point (i.e. index) 
to check for others within its window of occurrence or recurrence.
By default, this is always the earliest event within a `strata`. However, 
there are several ways to change this to suit different case definitions.  

## Direction of episode tracking
`from_last` determines if episodes tracking proceeds from the 
earliest to the most recent event or vice versa. Consequentially, this allows the 
selection of either the earliest or most recent event as the index event.

```{r warning=FALSE, fig.width=7}
# 3-day difference rolling episodes tracked in reverse
event_dt$ep5 <- episodes(
  event_dt$date, 3, episode_type = "rolling", from_last = TRUE, 
  group_stats = 'case_nm')
```

## Custom sorting
A custom preference for selecting index events can be provided to 
`custom_sort`. To demonstrate this, the example below uses `"RTI"` infections
as index events and then track episode forward or backward in time from the 
selected index event.

Custom sorting and the direction of episode tracking are implemented separately.
This allows both features to be combined to achieve specific outcomes or 
case definitions. As a result, the episodes which event belongs to can change 
in line with the requested settings. 

```{r warning=FALSE, fig.width=7}
# Custom preference
custom_pref <- ifelse(event_dt$attr_1 == "RTI", 1, 2)
# Track episode forward in time from index events
event_dt$ep6 <- episodes(
  event_dt$date, 3, custom_sort = custom_pref, skip_order = 1, 
  group_stats = 'case_nm')
# Track episode backward in time from index events
event_dt$ep7 <- episodes(
  event_dt$date, 3, custom_sort = custom_pref, skip_order = 1, from_last = TRUE, 
   group_stats = 'case_nm')

event_dt
```

It can also be useful to pair `skip_order` with `custom_sort`. `skip_order` will
stop the episode tracking process when all events up to rank-`n` of
your `custom_sort` has been tracked.

# Episode duration
Episode duration is primarily controlled by `case_length`.
However, `episodes()` offers more flexible ways to define episode duration and 
recurrence periods for complex case definitions. 

For example;

  + A different duration for recurrence from the `case_length`
can be passed to `recurrence_length`. 
  + A range ahead or before, and inclusive or not, of 
the index event can be used through a `number_line()` object. 
  + Multiple durations from an index event can also be checked by providing a list of
lengths or ranges as shown in the example below.
  + A different `case_length` or `recurrence_length` can be used for different events.

Each of these options for controlling episode duration and recurrence periods 
can be combined with preferential selection of index events in order to implement
a variety of case definitions.

```{r warning=FALSE, fig.width=7}
# 1-day difference occurrence period with 4-day difference recurrence periods
event_dt$ep8i <- episodes(
  event_dt$date, case_length = 1, recurrence_length = 4,  
  episode_type = "rolling", group_stats = 'case_nm')

# Rolling episodes with different periods of 
# occurrence and recurrence based on infection type
event_dt$ep8ii <- episodes(
  event_dt$date, case_length = event_dt$dur, episode_type = "rolling",
  group_stats = 'case_nm')

# Fixed episode within +/- 3 day-difference occurrence period from a
# preferentially selected index event 
event_dt$ep8ii <- episodes(
  event_dt$date, case_length = number_line(-3, 3), group_stats = 'case_nm', 
  episode_type = "fixed", custom_sort = custom_pref, skip_order = 1)

# Fixed episodes using occurrence windows of:
# -2 to -1, 4 to 5, and 7 to 9 days from the index event.
# Events falling between these windows are skipped.
event_dt$ep9 <- episodes(
  event_dt$date,  group_stats = 'case_nm',
  case_length = list(number_line(-2, -1), number_line(4, 5), number_line(7, 9)), 
  episode_type = "fixed", custom_sort = custom_pref, skip_order = 1, 
  skip_if_b4_lengths = TRUE)
event_dt
```

# Episodes from intervals

Episodes can be built from events with start and end times 
(event intervals) instead of a single point (date, time, numeric) in time. 
It should be noted that the reference point for event intervals is their end
point. Therefore, a `case_length` of `1` would be interpreted as 1-unit 
difference after the end point of the event. 

By default, events that occur within (but excluding the end point of) 
index event interval will not be captured. To capture them, 
use `index_window()` to get the range required to capture 
such events, and supply it to `case_length` or `recurrence_length`. 
See the examples below.

```{r warning=FALSE}
# Sample hospital stays
data(hospital_admissions)
event_int <- hospital_admissions['rd_id']
event_int$admin_period <- number_line(
    hospital_admissions$admin_dt, hospital_admissions$discharge_dt)
                                  
# Group overlapping hospital stays
event_int$ep1 <- episodes(
  date = event_int$admin_period, 
  case_length = index_window(event_int$admin_period),
  group_stats = 'case_nm')

# Group overlapping hospital stays and those within
# 20-day difference after the end point of the index hospital stay 
event_int$ep2 <- episodes(
  date = event_int$admin_period, 
  case_length = expand_number_line(
    index_window(event_int$admin_period), 20, "right"))
```

```{r warning=FALSE, fig.width=7}
event_int
```

## Overlap methods for event intervals
We can request that only event intervals which overlap in specific 
ways be built into the same episode. The overlap methods are passed to 
`case_overlap_methods` and `recurrence_overlap_methods`. 

Currently, `diyar` recognises 7 main mutually exclusive 
ways a pair of intervals can overlap. Multiple methods can be requested by 
separating each with a vertical bar. Please see `vignette("number_line")` 
and `help(overlaps)` for more details about this. 

```{r warning=FALSE}
# Wrapper function for a fixed episode
episodes_wf <- function(x){
  epids <- episodes(date = event_int$admin_period, 
                    sn = event_int$rd_id, 
                    case_length = index_window(event_int$admin_period), 
                    case_overlap_methods = x,
                    group_stats = 'case_nm')
  return(epids)
}

# Methods 
methods <- list(
  # Identical intervals
  exact = "exact",
  # Intervals with their start or end points within another
  across = "across",
  # Intervals with aligned start points
  aligns_start = "aligns_start",
  # Intervals with aligned end points
  aligns_end = "aligns_end",
  # Intervals with start points that align with the end point of another, and vice versa
  chain = "chain",
  # Intervals occurring completely within others
  inbetween = "inbetween",
  # A combination of `chain` and `inbetween` methods
  cb1 = "chain|inbetween",
  # A combination of `exact`, `chain` and `inbetween` methods
  cb2 = "exact|chain|inbetween",
  # A combination of `across`, `chain` and `aligns_end` methods
  cb3 = "across|chain|aligns_end"
)

epids <- event_int['admin_period']
for(m in methods){
  epids[[m]] <- episodes_wf(m)
}

# Use `schema()` to visualise each.
epids
```

Combining `case_overlap_methods` and `recurrence_overlap_methods` with 
`case_length` and `recurrence__length` gives a lot of flexibility in determining
how event intervals should overlap. For example, the examples below are different 
ways of the achieving the same outcome of linking the first two records.  

```{r warning=FALSE}
# Group hospital stays with the same start point (aligns_start) or 
# same start and end points (exact).
event_int$ep3 <- episodes(
  date = event_int$admin_period, 
  case_length = index_window(event_int$admin_period),
  case_overlap_methods = 'aligns_start|exact', group_stats = 'case_nm')

# Group hospital stays that overlap at any point within 9-day difference
# before the end point of the index event interval.
event_int$ep4 <- episodes(
  date = event_int$admin_period, case_length = number_line(-9,-9),
  case_overlap_methods = 'overlap', group_stats = 'case_nm')

event_int
```

# Additional match criteria
`episodes()` can apply additional match criteria when building episodes. 
This means only events that fall within requested period of occurrence or 
recurrence, and also meets the specified conditions will be assigned to the 
same episode. The match criteria are created as a `sub_criteria` object and
passed to `case_sub_criteria` and `recurrence_sub_criteria`. 
Please see `vignette("links")` for more details about `sub_criteria` objects. 

In the example below, we specify that only index
events that are an `"RTI"` or occurred in `"Ward 3"` can start an episode.
```{r warning=FALSE, fig.width=7}
# Sub-criteria 1 - RTI or Ward 2 index events only
match_funx1 <- function(x, y) y == "RTI"
match_funx2 <- function(x, y) y == "Ward 2"
sub_cri_1 <- sub_criteria(
  event_dt$attr_1, event_dt$attr_2, operator = "or", 
  match_funcs = c(match_funx1, match_funx2))

event_dt$ep10 <- episodes(
  event_dt$date, case_length = 5, case_sub_criteria = sub_cri_1)

schema(event_dt$ep10, seed = tmp.seed, show_labels = c("length_arrow"),
       custom_label = paste0(event_dt$attr_1, " in ", event_dt$attr_2))
```

Alternatively, we can request that `"BSI"` events or those that occurred in 
`"Ward 1"` should not be linked to any episode. Note that they will still be 
able to start episodes of their own unless otherwise specified as with
`event_dt$ep10`.   
```{r warning=FALSE, fig.width=7}
# Sub-criteria 2 - Exclude BSI and Ward 1 events 
match_funx3 <- function(x, y) !(x$attr_1 == "BSI" | x$attr_2 == "Ward 1")
sub_cri_2 <- sub_criteria(
  attrs(attr_1 = event_dt$attr_1, 
        attr_2 = event_dt$attr_2), 
        operator = "and", match_funcs = match_funx3, equal_funcs = diyar::true)

event_dt$ep11 <- episodes(
  event_dt$date, case_length = 5, case_sub_criteria = sub_cri_2)

schema(event_dt$ep11, seed = tmp.seed, show_labels = c("length_arrow"),
       custom_label = paste0(event_dt$attr_1, " in ", event_dt$attr_2))
```

We can even combine both conditions into a nested condition.
```{r warning=FALSE, fig.width=7}
combined_sub_cri <- sub_criteria(sub_cri_1, sub_cri_2, operator = "and")
event_dt$ep12 <- episodes(
  event_dt$date, case_length = 5, case_sub_criteria = combined_sub_cri)

schema(event_dt$ep12, seed = tmp.seed, show_labels = c("length_arrow"),
       custom_label = paste0(event_dt$attr_1, " in ", event_dt$attr_2))
```
